answers.name: Ramen
answers.fact: Japan has a whole museum for it: the Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum.

answers.name: Pad thai
answers.fact: Promoted as a national dish by the Thai government in the 1930s and 40s.

answers.name: Chow mein
answers.fact: The name means 'stir-fried noodles' in Cantonese.

answers.name: Lo mein
answers.fact: 'Tossed noodles': boiled, then tossed in sauce rather than fried crisp.

answers.name: Instant noodles
answers.fact: Invented by Momofuku Ando in 1958. The world now eats over 100 billion servings a year.

answers.name: Chicken noodle soup
answers.fact: Campbell's 1934 original was called 'Chicken with Noodles'.

answers.name: Pho
answers.fact: Said closer to 'fuh' than 'foe', and traditionally eaten for breakfast.

answers.name: Japchae
answers.fact: Made with sweet potato glass noodles, which were only added in the 20th century.

answers.name: Dan dan noodles
answers.fact: Named after the shoulder pole ('dan') Sichuan street vendors carried them on.

answers.name: Udon
answers.fact: Kagawa prefecture brands itself 'Udon Prefecture'.

answers.name: Soba
answers.fact: Made from buckwheat, which isn't actually related to wheat.

answers.name: Laksa
answers.fact: A coconut-curry noodle soup from the Peranakan kitchens of Malaysia and Singapore.

answers.name: Singapore noodles
answers.fact: Barely known in Singapore. It's a Cantonese restaurant invention.

answers.name: Pad see ew
answers.fact: The name means 'stir-fried with soy sauce'.

answers.name: Drunken noodles
answers.fact: Nobody agrees on the name: hangover cure, or just that much chilli?

answers.name: Yakisoba
answers.fact: Despite the 'soba', it's made with wheat noodles, not buckwheat.

answers.name: Hokkien mee
answers.fact: Singapore's is a prawn-and-squid fry-up; Kuala Lumpur's is dark and soy-braised.

answers.name: Char kway teow
answers.fact: Traditionally fried in pork lard with cockles over a roaring wok.

answers.name: Mee goreng
answers.fact: Literally 'fried noodles' in Malay and Indonesian.

answers.name: Ramyeon
answers.fact: South Koreans eat some of the most instant noodles per person on Earth.

answers.name: Jajangmyeon
answers.fact: On 'Black Day', 14 April, single Koreans eat it to commiserate.

answers.name: Somen
answers.fact: Served cold in summer, sometimes sent down a bamboo flume for you to catch.

answers.name: Chow fun
answers.fact: Judged on 'wok hei', the smoky breath of a very hot wok.

answers.name: Wonton noodle soup
answers.fact: Classic Hong Kong bowls hide a spoon at the bottom to keep the noodles from going soggy.

answers.name: Beef noodle soup
answers.fact: Taipei holds an annual festival just for it.

answers.name: Hakka noodles
answers.fact: An Indo-Chinese favourite from Kolkata's Chinese community.

answers.name: Pancit
answers.fact: A Filipino birthday staple: long noodles for a long life.

answers.name: Spätzle
answers.fact: German egg noodles scraped off a board straight into boiling water.

answers.name: Tsukemen
answers.fact: Dipping ramen, invented in Tokyo in 1955: cold noodles, hot thick broth.

answers.name: Hiyashi chuka
answers.fact: Chilled ramen salad. Shops put up signs when it's back for summer.

answers.name: Champon
answers.fact: Nagasaki's seafood noodle soup, first made for Chinese students around 1900.

answers.name: Tantanmen
answers.fact: Japan's soupier spin on Sichuan dan dan noodles.

answers.name: Abura soba
answers.fact: Brothless 'oil' ramen you season yourself with vinegar and chilli oil.

answers.name: Naengmyeon
answers.fact: Cold buckwheat noodles in icy broth, often snipped with scissors at the table.

answers.name: Kalguksu
answers.fact: The name means 'knife noodles': the dough is cut by hand.

answers.name: Jjamppong
answers.fact: The spicy seafood twin of jajangmyeon at Korean-Chinese restaurants.

answers.name: Budae jjigae
answers.fact: 'Army stew', built from US base surplus like Spam after the Korean War, with ramen on top.

answers.name: Khao soi
answers.fact: Northern Thai curry noodle soup with a crown of crispy fried noodles.

answers.name: Boat noodles
answers.fact: Once sold from canal boats in tiny bowls you order by the stack.

answers.name: Pad woon sen
answers.fact: Stir-fried glass noodles made from mung bean starch.

answers.name: Rad na
answers.fact: Wide rice noodles under a thick, glossy gravy.

answers.name: Bún chả
answers.fact: Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain shared a famous bowl in Hanoi in 2016.

answers.name: Bún bò Huế
answers.fact: Spicy lemongrass beef noodle soup from Vietnam's old imperial capital.

answers.name: Bún riêu
answers.fact: The broth gets its flavour from pounded freshwater crab.

answers.name: Hủ tiếu
answers.fact: A southern Vietnamese noodle soup with Chinese-Cambodian roots.

answers.name: Assam laksa
answers.fact: Penang's sour tamarind-and-mackerel laksa. No coconut milk at all.

answers.name: Mee siam
answers.fact: Sweet-sour rice vermicelli whose name means 'Siamese noodles'.

answers.name: Mee rebus
answers.fact: 'Boiled noodles' in a thick, sweet potato-based gravy.

answers.name: Pan mee
answers.fact: Hand-torn Hakka noodles; the name means 'board noodles'.

answers.name: Mie ayam
answers.fact: Indonesian chicken noodles, sold from carts all over Jakarta.

answers.name: Thukpa
answers.fact: A Tibetan noodle soup eaten right across the Himalayas.

answers.name: Falooda
answers.fact: A dessert drink of vermicelli, rose syrup and basil seeds, with Persian roots.

answers.name: Idiyappam
answers.fact: Rice dough pressed into lacy nests and steamed, from South India and Sri Lanka.

answers.name: Zhajiangmian
answers.fact: Beijing's 'fried sauce noodles', ancestor of Korea's jajangmyeon.

answers.name: Lanzhou beef noodles
answers.fact: Hand-pulled to order: one lump of dough becomes hundreds of strands in seconds.

answers.name: Knife-cut noodles
answers.fact: Shanxi cooks shave the dough straight into the pot with a curved blade.

answers.name: Longevity noodles
answers.fact: A Chinese birthday dish. Biting them short is bad luck.

answers.name: Cold sesame noodles
answers.fact: A Chinese street snack that became a New York takeaway classic.

answers.name: Scallion oil noodles
answers.fact: A Shanghai classic: noodles, soy and scallions fried crisp in oil. That's it.

answers.name: Tuna noodle casserole
answers.fact: A 1950s American potluck staple, held together by canned soup.

answers.name: Noodle kugel
answers.fact: A baked Jewish egg-noodle pudding, sweet or savoury.

answers.name: Fideuà
answers.fact: Paella's cousin from Valencia, made with short noodles instead of rice.

answers.name: Lagman
answers.fact: Hand-pulled noodles carried across Central Asia by the Uyghurs and Dungans.

answers.name: Koshari
answers.fact: Egypt's national dish piles noodles, rice, lentils and macaroni together.

answers.name: Saimin
answers.fact: Hawaii's own noodle soup, born on the plantations from several Asian cuisines.

answers.name: Mohinga
answers.fact: Myanmar's unofficial national dish: rice noodles in fish broth, for breakfast.

answers.name: Cao lầu
answers.fact: Tradition says the real thing needs water from one particular well in Hội An.

answers.name: Guilin rice noodles
answers.fact: Guilin's breakfast, topped with crispy pork and pickled beans.

answers.name: Ants climbing a tree
answers.fact: Glass noodles with minced pork. The pork bits are the 'ants'.

answers.name: Beshbarmak
answers.fact: Kazakhstan's national dish. The name means 'five fingers': you eat it by hand.

answers.name: Hot dry noodles
answers.fact: Wuhan's breakfast of choice, tossed in sesame paste with no soup at all.

answers.name: Biang biang noodles
answers.fact: Its Chinese character takes around 58 strokes to write.
